clue.text: 50% healthy, not completely fine at first

indicators.note: the word for healthy is not given in full, losing its last letter

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in 'hale and hearty'

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word fine is used

explanation.surface: Someone only half well, not quite fine to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely' cuts HALE to HAL; 'at first' gives F from 'fine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifty per cent is one of two equal parts of a whole.

clue.text: A popular plant for a racecourse

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a tree is a plant

explanation.surface: A well-liked shrub chosen to decorate a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous British horse-racing venue, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Female to startle in a dress

parts.note: to rock is to shake or shock, so startle

explanation.surface: A woman given a fright while wearing a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A frock is a woman's or girl's dress, a near synonym.

clue.text: Church the Italian put in primary area

indicators.note: the Italian article is placed inside the word for primary

parts.note: basic means primary or fundamental
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: An Italian setting a church in a main district.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, especially one given special privileges by the Pope.

clue.text: Prohibit regular extraction from brain?

indicators.note: taking every other letter from the word brain, starting with its first

explanation.surface: A question whether regular removal of brain tissue should be forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular extraction from' takes letters 1, 3 and 5 of 'brain'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban something is to forbid it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Concern in South Carolina over line that's frightening?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part is placed above the next
the word for concern sits inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for the US state of South Carolina
care means concern or worry
a row is a line

explanation.surface: Worry in South Carolina about a frightening queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' works because this is a down entry: SCAREC sits above ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow is a figure set up in fields to frighten off birds, hence something meant to frighten.

clue.text: Article is probing hero's love affair

indicators.note: the article and 'is' push into the word for hero

parts.note: a lion is a brave person or hero, as in a literary lion
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper story digs into a celebrity's romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic or sexual relationship.

clue.text: Drink companies start to advertise

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, twice for the plural

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word advertise

explanation.surface: Firms begin promoting a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot drink made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: You won't be caught napping with this

definitions.text: You won't be caught napping with this

parts.words: You won't be caught napping with this
parts.note: 'caught napping' usually means caught off guard, but read literally it means you cannot sleep

explanation.surface: Advice on something that keeps you alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering sleeplessness never manages to doze off, so is never found asleep.

clue.text: Support walk, heading off …

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for walk is removed

parts.note: to march is to walk in step

explanation.surface: Backing for a protest walk that is setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curved structure that holds up the weight above it.

clue.text: …long walk to reach Eastern Kinross, initially

indicators.note: the first letters of the four words to, reach, Eastern, Kinross

explanation.surface: A lengthy hike to get to the eastern part of Kinross, a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 9 across; 'initially' applies to all four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, arduous journey on foot.

clue.text: Church title recalled when including a couple of Saints and Bishop?

indicators.note: the reversed word for title takes in the two letters for saints
the word for title is called back, so read backwards

parts.note: a name is a title
S is the abbreviation for saint, so two of them

explanation.surface: A church honorific remembered with two saints and a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns the title backwards to EMAN. Bishop looks like a clergyman to match the church, but the question mark flags it as a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is one of the pieces used in chess, so an example of the definition.

clue.text: Fraudulent player keen to support comical character

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting part goes underneath

parts.note: a card is a funny, eccentric person
sharp means keen, as of a blade

explanation.surface: An eager fan backing a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a cheat who wins at card games by trickery.

clue.text: Ruin part of garden when reversing? I'm expected to pay

indicators.note: the two words are put together and then read backwards

parts.note: rot is decay, ruin
a flower bed is part of a garden

explanation.surface: A gardener backing a car destroys a flowerbed and expects a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: ROT plus BED gives ROTBED, which reads backwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A debtor is a person who owes money and so is due to pay it back.

clue.text: Pooh's friend is about right to set off

indicators.note: the friend's name goes around the letter for right

parts.note: Tigger is the bouncy tiger friend of Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh's pal is about to start off.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to start it or cause it to happen.

clue.text: Fame about now, heading for notoriety

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word notoriety

explanation.surface: A remark on celebrity today turning into infamy.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is the state of being widely known and honoured, a synonym of celebrity.

clue.text: We swallow the bait, hogging second spot on the Net

indicators.note: the word for taking the bait holds the letter for second inside it

parts.note: to bite is to take the bait

explanation.surface: Fish that gulp the lure and greedily take a spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A website is a location on the internet, so a place online.

clue.text: Many shops recognised item of hardware

parts.note: a chain is a group of shops under one owner
saw means recognised or perceived

explanation.surface: A retail group spotted a piece of equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A chainsaw is a powered cutting tool, the kind of thing sold by a hardware store.

clue.text: Home, seeing us in garden

indicators.note: the word us is placed inside the verb for gardening

parts.note: to hoe is to work the ground, so to garden

explanation.surface: Back at home, spotting us in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden' is a verb here, not the noun it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: A house is a building people live in, a dwelling.

clue.text: Secures new muscles

parts.note: abs are the abdominal muscles

explanation.surface: Someone at the gym gets freshly toned stomach muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab is to catch or grab, so secures in the sense of seizes.

clue.text: Skill, by the sound of it? Definitely not

indicators.note: the entry is spoken just like the word for skill

parts.note: know-how is practical skill or expertise

explanation.surface: A doubtful question about ability answered with a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is a colloquial way of saying in no way at all.

clue.text: Virus containing note getting illicit payment

indicators.note: the word for virus holds the letter for note

parts.note: a bug is an informal word for a virus

explanation.surface: A computer virus carrying a message that triggers a corrupt payout.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNG is British slang for a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is a bribe, a payment made to secure improper favour.

clue.text: Spider rain had disturbed, securing cover initially

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the next letter inside them
the letters of rain had are shaken into a new order
the opening letter of the word cover

explanation.surface: A spider troubled by the rain takes shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges RAIN HAD to ARAHNID; 'securing' puts C, from 'cover' via 'initially', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders belong to the class of eight-legged creatures that also includes scorpions and mites.

clue.text: Agreement with no power in law

indicators.note: the word for agreement is used without the letter for power

parts.note: a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: A treaty that has no legal force.
explanation.definitionFit: An act is a statute passed by a parliament, so a piece of legislation.

clue.text: Reduced order? Mine will become dilapidated

indicators.note: the word for order loses its last letter

parts.note: a decree is an official order
a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: A cut-back command means a colliery will fall into disrepair.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means worn out and falling apart through age or neglect.

clue.text: Little kindergarten's opening in seven days

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: the first letter of the word kindergarten

explanation.surface: A small child's first week at kindergarten.
explanation.definitionFit: A week is the period of seven days.
